question: Does every number in the PAPER-FINAL close-out have a claim row (or an explicit recompute key) behind it?
answer: NO — 17 of 314 distinct numeric tokens in the close-out have no claim row behind them; 4 of the 17 are wrong or unprovable, 2 readings are wrong, and the guarded 277 are row-exact. Most of the misses are not new: the close-out inherited them because it folded older prose (abstract, 6a, 10, 11) into new sections.
checks: Mapped all 314 distinct numeric tokens in the close-out (§8a L481-531, §9c/§9d L694-789, §10 rules+null L800-851, the abstract and closing paragraph L8-96, §11 carried gaps) to a CLAIMS.md row and/or a recompute/recompute_r2 expected key.

Re-ran every guard the close-out cites: verify_package PASS, recompute all 64 PASS lines + coverage guard PASS, recompute_r2 C64 38/38 C65 48/48 C66 75/75 C67 85/85 C68 70/70 SYSOPT 50/50, recompute_r2 redgreen 4/4, serving_brief --check PASS (19 items, 13 cells), pytest tests/ 1368 passed 1 skipped.

Re-derived the four figures that had no key from the raw rows with my own arithmetic (P2-REPAD rows: extra cached 70 pairs mean 74.0571 with 9/41/20 split; pad 71 rows 6,737 mean 94.8873; prompt_tokens 875,856 / 163,311 / 170,048; G3-LIMIT-V2 2,780 rows x 6 arms of 350 with F-k800 at 2,330).
Ruled on the two items PAPER-FINAL itself flagged as overstated, and on the arithmetic claims the close-out added.
not_reproduced: §9c/§9d 'the dense-vLLM cell's hot-token gcd is 16' and §11 'the other's is 16, below a page' — does not reproduce: C65's own expected value is dense/vLLM 879.0669 uncached per turn, and C65 and C63 both carry hot gcd 1,088 for that cell. A cell that pays 879 uncached tokens per turn cannot have a hot-hit gcd of 16; 64 divides 1,088, so a 64-grid residue is exactly what that cell would show. Nothing in recompute or recompute_r2 keys a gcd of 16, so the sentence is unguarded as well as unreproduced.

§9c 'the same 1,136 rows, re-derived independently of recompute.py, into a second script' — the document declaring the sources is CLAIMS.md column 4 ('`.venv/bin/python papers/context-cache/recompute_r2.py C65`') and READER-MAP.md row C65 ('papers/context-cache/recompute_r2.py ... MOE-VLLM, G3, R2-PROMPT, DENSE-SGL'). The independent-re-derivation claim is therefore contradicted by the map the package enforces.

§8a table column headed 'prompt bytes' with 12,336 / 2,300 / 2,395 — the figures reproduce as prompt TOKENS from the rows (mean prompt_tokens 12,336.0 / 2,300.1549 / 2,395.0423 over 71 turns each; state/r2-p2-repad.json stores the same three) but no byte count exists anywhere in the package: the rows carry prompt_tokens and prompt_sha256 and no char/byte field. A 12,336-token prompt is ~43 KB at this cell's own token_ratio_chars 0.2836, so 'bytes' is off by a factor of ~3.5. The label is wrong and the column has no claim row.

§8a 'which is why the pad over the 70 countable rows is 6,643 / 94.90' — the ratio is a coincidence of the denominator. 6,643 is tokens of extra cache over 70 PAIRS (mean 74.0571), not a pad, and the true pad over all 71 P2 rows is 6,737 / 94.8873 (the cell's own figure); 70 x 94.90 = 6,643.0 is the pad that a 70-row denominator would IMPLY. The manuscript's framing presents the implied pad as if it were the sum of the pad rows.

§9d 'a per-turn cost of about twenty-four tokens is roughly 1.4 % of the bill' — arithmetic only (23.5211 / 1,664.3521 = 1.413 %), and neither operand combination is checked by any guard; it is commentary, not the defect.
overstated: PAPER-FINAL's own flag on O3 is CORRECT and its second flag is NOT: 'pays +55.65' on O3 describes a null (+55.6479 [-136.493, +246.014], excludes_zero False), so the word should be withdrawn; but PANEL's '19/20 and 19/20 -> 18/20' is right — state/sys-opt-v1.json carries stored_mismatches 20/20 (MoE before and after) and 19/20 -> 18/20 (dense), so PANEL is the one that should be fixed.

§9d 'That is the cheapest direct evidence in this paper that a mid-run edit of a cached prefix is paid for per turn, not once at the edit' — one of the four setups supports it, and three are nulls straddling zero. The sentence reads a result off the setup that produced it. It is the same defect class as the withdrawn 'null on all four', in the opposite direction.
unverified: §10 'the ceiling was reached by the stop rule and not by exhausting the design' — 'three budgeted rounds', 'round 2 requires a DECISIONS entry' and 'rounds 2-3 were unspent, which is not headroom' are process facts with no CLAIMS.md row; the only machine-readable trace is state/sys-opt-v1.json, whose protocol carries rows_expected 426 / rows_measured 426 and live_requests_used 565 (bound 500) and tool_calls 39 (bound 30).

§10 drift control '63.15 (MoE) and 13.13 (dense)' — reproduces from state/sys-opt-v1.json (63.15493 / 13.12676) but is NOT in the SYSOPT recompute key set (grep on recompute_r2.py finds neither number), so no command re-derives it.

§8a '68 of that arm's 71 rows were second sends' — reproduced from cells/R2-PROMPT/O3-REPEAT/rows.jsonl (68 rows carry pad_corrections 1, 3 carry 0) but unguarded by any recompute key; the same paragraph runs two count systems in one breath, the withdrawn cell's 68 vs the replacement P2-REPAD's 0 (213 rows x requests_sent 1).

§6a/§10 'every arm has turns below its baseline' and §6a 'at least one turn below its baseline' — C62 recompute says post_turns_below_zero 12 of 12, contradicted by §11's '11 of 12 arms contain at least one turn below their baseline'. 12 is the correct figure; §11 is the stale one.
PAPER-FINAL's claimed edit count 'five edits in MANUSCRIPT.md' — its artifact list itself enumerates seven fold sites (8a, 9c, 9d, rule 5, 11, the abstract closing sentence AND a C63 sign repair).

§6a 'twelve arm means over 27-89 turns each' and §11 'post-boundary averages cover 47 to 89 turns' — both bands are the same twelve means seen from different ends (means are taken over 27-89 turns, medians/transitions over 47-89); the second needs its noun fixed.

PANEL §11 'The optimisation round is closed ... listed as an open gap in GAPS.md G4' with §10 'the null recorded at the end of this section' — GAPS.md carries no G4 line for the SYS-OPT carried gaps, and §10 carries no such null; the signposts do not land.

Proven against the author's guards instead: planting the probe clause back on MANUSCRIPT.md:96 left pytest (ledger + attribution guard + matrix fold) at 26/26 PASS and verify_package at PASS, which is a MEASURED GUARD GAP — no guard covers the closing sentence, and none guards the prompt-bytes column, the hot-gcd 16, or the drift control.

assumptions: No board card and no waiver names this session, so the unit name is carried from the prompt ('PAPER-FINAL-V2B') and the handoff is written by the session doing the work.

'The new close-out' is read as the PAPER-FINAL close (MANUSCRIPT §8a/§9c/§9d/§10/§11, the abstract closing sentence, GAPS G17) rather than as a section titled V2B, which does not exist anywhere in the package (grep for V2B across papers/, experiments/, state/ and orchestration/ returns nothing outside this unit's own name).

A number counts as 'having a claim row behind it' when a CLAIMS.md row (or its recompute key set, reached through READER-MAP.md) carries it or a figure it is arithmetically derived from; commentary, counts and budget ceilings need a row too, which is where most of the 17 misses come from.
